full.description: This is a low-power photomicrograph of cross-sections of the small intestine. The histological sections demonstrate transmural inflammation, with thickening of the intestinal wall, lymphoid aggregates, and architectural distortion. These findings are characteristic of regional enteritis, also known as Crohn's disease.

blind.description: This is a gross pathology specimen of the small intestine. The tissue exhibits thickened walls, mucosal cobblestoning, and deep ulceration characteristic of regional enteritis. These transmural inflammatory changes are typical of Crohn's disease affecting the small bowel. The findings demonstrate the hallmark chronic inflammatory features of this gastrointestinal condition.

random.description: This is a low-magnification photomicrograph of tissue sections, likely representing colon or intestinal mucosa. The image shows varying degrees of mucosal architecture and pathology across multiple tissue fragments. On the right, there is a prominent exophytic mass showing architectural distortion and invasion through the muscular layer. These features are consistent with an invasive carcinoma, such as an adenocarcinoma of the colon.
